beginner.summary: For system administrators, developers and junior cloud or network engineers who run web applications but have not designed load balancing themselves. Covers what a load balancer does at Layer 4 and Layer 7, balancing algorithms, active and passive health checks, session persistence, TLS termination and passthrough, client IP preservation, timeouts and retries, connection draining, an HAProxy pair made highly available with Keepalived, a first look at AWS, Azure and Google Cloud load balancers and Kubernetes Services, and reading load balancer logs and 5xx errors, ending with a highly available web tier capstone.
prerequisites: Explains IP addresses, ports, TCP and the basic HTTP request and response cycle
Works on a Linux command line: editing files, systemctl, curl and reading logs under /var/log
Has a laptop with Docker and Docker Compose able to run six or more small containers, plus a free-tier account on at least one public cloud
outcomes: Choose between a Layer 4 and a Layer 7 load balancer and a suitable algorithm for a given workload
Configure HAProxy with health checks, cookie persistence, TLS termination and graceful server draining
Build a two-node HAProxy pair with a Keepalived virtual IP that survives the loss of either node
Diagnose 502, 503 and 504 responses from load balancer logs and map each to its likely cause
